title: Solar System Cadet Challenge
description: Test your fundamental knowledge about spacecraft, planets, and NASA's greatest missions!

questions.question_text: What is the farthest human-made object from Earth?
options: Curiosity Rover
Voyager 1
Hubble Space Telescope
Apollo 11 Lunar Module
questions.explanation: Voyager 1 was launched in 1977 and entered interstellar space in 2012. It is currently over 24 billion kilometers (165 AU) from Earth!
questions.fun_fact: A radio signal travelling at the speed of light takes over 22 hours to reach Voyager 1 from Earth.

questions.question_text: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet' and has hosted rovers like Curiosity and Perseverance?
options: Venus
Jupiter
Mars
Mercury
questions.explanation: Mars gets its reddish color from iron oxide (rust) covering its surface rocks and regolith.
questions.fun_fact: Olympus Mons on Mars is the largest volcano in the solar system, three times taller than Mount Everest!

questions.question_text: How did the Perseverance rover land safely on Mars without crashing?
options: Bouncing air bags like a giant beach ball
A rocket-powered Sky Crane that lowered it on nylon cables
It landed in an ocean of liquid water
It glided down with wings like an airplane
questions.explanation: Because Perseverance weighs over 1,000 kg, NASA used a rocket-powered Sky Crane to gently lower it onto its wheels in Jezero Crater.
questions.fun_fact: The landing took 7 minutes, but communication took 11 minutes to reach Earth, meaning the rover was already safe before scientists knew!

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the Apollo 11 Lunar Ranging Retroreflector left on the Moon in 1969?
options: To reflect sunlight to melt ice
To bounce laser beams from Earth to measure the exact distance to the Moon
To transmit television signals
To power the rover battery
questions.explanation: The retroreflector is an array of corner prisms that bounce laser pulses straight back to Earth observatories, measuring the Moon's distance to millimeter precision.
questions.fun_fact: This experiment proved that the Moon is moving 3.8 centimeters farther away from Earth each year!

title: Deep Space Explorer Challenge
description: Demonstrate your understanding of deep space propulsion, nuclear power, and ocean worlds!

questions.question_text: Why do deep space probes like Voyager 1, Cassini, and New Horizons use RTGs instead of solar panels?
options: Solar panels are too heavy for rockets to launch
The Sun's light is too weak billions of kilometers away in the outer solar system
Solar panels attract dangerous space dust
Nuclear batteries generate infinite electricity forever
questions.explanation: Sunlight follows the inverse-square law. At Saturn and Pluto, sunlight is hundreds or thousands of times weaker than on Earth, making solar panels ineffective.
questions.fun_fact: RTGs use the natural decay heat of Plutonium-238 converted into electricity by thermocouples with no moving parts.

questions.question_text: Why did NASA deliberately steer the Cassini spacecraft into Saturn's atmosphere at the end of its mission?
options: Because its thrusters were broken
To protect ocean moons Enceladus and Titan from potential microbial contamination
To ignite Saturn's gas clouds
To break the off-world speed record
questions.explanation: Cassini discovered that Enceladus has a warm subsurface ocean capable of harboring life. NASA crashed Cassini into Saturn so Earth bacteria could never contaminate Enceladus.
questions.fun_fact: This protocol is known as Planetary Protection, established under the international Outer Space Treaty.

questions.question_text: What is a 'gravity assist' (slingshot maneuver) in space navigation?
options: Using a planet's gravity and orbital momentum to speed up or redirect a spacecraft without burning fuel
Throwing heavy weights off the back of the spacecraft
Deploying a giant parachute in planetary atmospheres
Turning off the engine to let gravity pull you into the Sun
questions.explanation: A spacecraft steals a tiny sliver of a planet's orbital momentum as it swings around it, dramatically boosting its velocity through space.
questions.fun_fact: Voyager 2 used gravity assists from Jupiter, Saturn, and Uranus to reach Neptune in just 12 years instead of 30!
